section.title: Appending or replacing a scan protocol
section.hierarchy_path: /Examination/Preparations/Calling up the Patient Model Dialog/Appending or replacing a scan protocol

semantic_nodes.canonical_text: Appending or replacing a scan protocol
In the Patient Model Dialog, you can append or replace the current scan protocol with another scan protocol.
Modifications are only valid for the current examination. The predefined scan protocol will not be changed. Each scan protocol can contain up to 100 entries.

The Append and Replace options are only operable when at least one scan protocol has been loaded into the chronicle. The selected scan protocol will be added after, or instead of, the current protocol.
1 Click the Select or change exam icon to open the Patient Model Dialog .
2 Select Append to append the protocols.
– or –
Select Replace to replace the entries of the current scan protocol with the newly selected scan protocol.
The new protocol will be created. The not yet executed protocol steps will be deleted.
3 Click the respective body part of the displayed graphic or the buttons for the special scan protocol (for example, Cardiac , Specials, or RT).
A list of scan protocols is displayed.
Force / Force Velo | Instructions for Use Print No. C2-058-C.621.01.01.02
SOMATOM | syngo CT VB30 268
6 Examination
4 Mark the relevant name in the list of the scan protocols.

section.title: Series descriptions of FAST DE Results series
section.hierarchy_path: /Examination/Preparations/Using automatic functions/Automatic postprocessing of Dual Energy images/Series descriptions of FAST DE Results series

semantic_nodes.canonical_text: 6 Examination
Series descriptions of FAST DE Results series
The Series description of the FAST DE Series is generated based on your entry in the Output series description field.
To your entry the following suffix is added:
<Filter name> of the selected Dual Energy application class, for example, Mono40
The Series description may be, for example, Arterial Mono40 .
If you leave the Output series description field empty, the name of the original reconstruction is used, with the following suffixes:
<Filter name> of the selected Dual Energy application class, for example, Mono40
_S<series number of the first series>_S<series number of the second series>_1 for the series numbers of both of the two original reconstructions
The Series description may be, for example, DE_Abdomen 5.0 D30f Mono40_S2_S3_1 .

section.title: Application class Virtual Unenhanced and FAST DE Results in Dual Energy reconstructions
section.hierarchy_path: /Examination/Preparations/Using automatic functions/Automatic postprocessing of Dual Energy images/Application classes/Application class Virtual Unenhanced and FAST DE Results in Dual Energy reconstructions

semantic_nodes.canonical_text: Application class Virtual Unenhanced and FAST DE Results in Dual Energy reconstructions
Observe the following limitations:

CT values of bone and calcifications will be lower in VNC (virtual non-contrast) images than in true non-contrast images. Small calcifications below 3 mm in diameter may not be visible in the VNC image.
Differences between CT values in VNC images and true non-contrast images are typically within ±10 HU.
The Virtual Unenhanced application class should not be used for images of the heart that were acquired without ECG-gating or triggering.
For a reliable evaluation of CT values of soft-tissue lesions on the Virtual Unenhanced application class image, ROI diameter should at least be 10 mm.
The CT value of subcutaneous and visceral fat will be higher in the VNC image than in the true non-contrast image.
The VNC image may not be appropriate for characterization of lesions where the presence or absence of fat is of clinical concern, for example adrenal tumors.

section.title: Positioning the arm supports
section.hierarchy_path: /Examination/Positioning the patient/Preparing the patient table/Positioning the mattress/Positioning the arm supports

semantic_nodes.canonical_text: Positioning the arm supports
The arm supports are placed under the patient and fixed by the patient's weight. The arm supports should be positioned outside the scan area, if possible.
CAUTION
Use of the mattress with flat surface!
Contusion of patient's fingers during table movement.
◆ Always use both arm supports with the mattress with flat surface.
◆ Observe that the hands of the patient are completely covered by the arm support.
◆ Always fix and observe the patient during table movement.
The patient is correctly positioned.
1 Slightly lift the patient at the level of his or her arms.
2 Push the first arm support with its flat side into the space between patient and table.
3 Position the arm support in a way that the patient's arm lies tight and comfortable against his or her body.
4 Ensure that the patient's hand is completely covered by the arm support.
5 Proceed to position the second arm support on the other side of the patient's body similarly.
After finishing the examination, the arm supports must be removed before the patient gets up from the table.
Force / Force Velo | Instructions for Use Print No. C2-058-C.621.01.01.02
SOMATOM | syngo CT VB30

section.title: Using the flaps and the restraint straps
section.hierarchy_path: /Examination/Positioning the patient/Preparing the patient/Using the flaps and the restraint straps

semantic_nodes.canonical_text: Using the flaps and the restraint straps
The patient is positioned on a mattress with spill protection.
◆ Close the flaps around the patient's body. If necessary, fix the flaps with one or more restraint straps.
The flaps are now protecting the table against body fluids.
The restraint straps are used to secure the flaps around the patient's body. They are not used to prevent the patient from falling off the table.
CAUTION
Incorrect use and use of non-original and non-released equipment!
Wrong diagnosis

◆ Use only the original accessories and equipment or equipment that is released by Siemens Healthineers. This includes, for example, phantoms, footswitches, ECG-cables, positioning aids, or table extensions.
◆ Use the released equipment exclusively for its original purpose.
◆ Always follow the instructions for use of the particular units used. This includes the labels applied on to the equipment as well as the instructions for use documents.
Force / Force Velo | Instructions for Use Print No. C2-058-C.621.01.01.02
SOMATOM | syngo CT VB30 286
6 Examination
WARNING
Incorrect use and use of non-original and non-released equipment!
Injury to the patient and personnel or damage to the equipment. Image quality may also decrease.

◆ Use only the original accessories and equipment or equipment that is released by Siemens Healthineers. This includes, for example, phantoms, footswitches, ECG-cables, positioning aids, or table extensions.
◆ Use the released equipment exclusively for its original purpose.
◆ Always follow the instructions for use of the particular units used. This includes the labels applied on to the equipment as well as the instructions for use documents.
WARNING
Incorrect patient positioning, unintended patient movement, and unobserved movement of the patient table or gantry!
Injury to the patient, for example, contusions of the patient's extremities and unusable radiation.
◆ Always fix the patient with accessories, as described in the instructions for use, to avoid unintentional patient movement. For example, use restraint straps and arm supports.

◆ Monitor the patient continuously as long as the table top and gantry are moving. Take special care if the tilt of the gantry is anything other than zero degrees or the table height is anything other than the isocenter.

◆ Make sure that nothing can get caught while the table or gantry are moving. For example, parts of the body or clothing, any needles, infusion tubes, respiration tubes, catheters, ECG cables, or sheets and blankets.
◆ Follow the markings and labels on the equipment.
◆ Press a STOP key if an injury to the patient can occur.

section.title: Setting the patient orientation
section.hierarchy_path: /Examination/Positioning the patient/Moving the patient to the scan start position/Setting the patient orientation

semantic_nodes.canonical_text: 6 Examination
Setting the patient orientation
When no scan protocol has been loaded before patient positioning, the orientation of the patient can be changed on the Touch Panel (Head first , Feet first) for correct patient positioning.
Check the position of the patient on the patient table. In case of mismatch, change the position on the positioning screen.
1 Tap the Rotate patient icon to change the orientation of the patient (Head first , Feet first).
2 Position the patient table for the scan. ( Page 178 Operation of the patient table)
3 After positioning the patient, confirm the patient position in the Patient Model Dialog at the console.
The Rotate patient icon is only visible when no scan protocol is loaded or the Camera Position mode is not active.

section.hierarchy_path: /Examination/Positioning the patient/Moving the patient to the scan start position/Checking the patient position/Centering the patient

semantic_nodes.canonical_text: Centering the patient
1 For optimum image quality and dose application to patient size and body shape with CARE Dose4D, position the patient in the isocenter of the gantry.
Force / Force Velo | Instructions for Use Print No. C2-058-C.621.01.01.02
SOMATOM | syngo CT VB30
6 Examination
2 Double-check and verify the position of the patient with the laser lightmarker as well as in the topogram.
If the patient is positioned too high, the mAs for the subsequent scan is increased.
If the patient is positioned too low, the mAs for the subsequent scan is reduced and the images show increased noise.
For head scans with Auto Isocenter, you may be prompted to raise or lower the patient table. This has no impact on the dose modulation with CARE Dose4D.

section.title: Taking a planning image
section.hierarchy_path: /Examination/Positioning the patient/Using the 3D camera/Taking a planning image

semantic_nodes.canonical_text: Taking a planning image
On the positioning screen, you can take a planning image of the patient.
The patient is positioned on the patient table directly below the camera system. ( Page 285 Preparing the patient)
Make sure that the entire patient, from head to toe and with sufficient additional clearance, is visible on the Touch Panel screen.
A live image of the patient is displayed on the positioning screen.
Force / Force Velo | Instructions for Use Print No. C2-058-C.621.01.01.02
SOMATOM | syngo CT VB30 293
6 Examination
(1) Camera icon
Shaded area
The shaded area represents the range which cannot be scanned.
You can take planning images at any vertical table position, even when a part of the Touch Panel screen is shaded.
1 Tap the Camera icon.
A planning image of the patient is captured and displayed on the positioning screen.
As the planning image is created, an algorithm runs in the background detecting the following points automatically:
Patient position (Head first , Feet first , prone / supine)
Body landmarks of the patient
Isocenter of the patient
Force / Force Velo | Instructions for Use Print No. C2-058-C.621.01.01.02
SOMATOM | syngo CT VB30 294
6 Examination
The body landmarks and the iso-center of the patient could not be detected and the Preset icons are dimmed.
◆ Position the patient directly below the camera and retake the planning image.
◆ Move away any device which obstructs the view on the patient and retake the planning image.
◆ Position the patient manually by using the movement keys on the gantry operator panel.
2 Optional: If you wish to retake a planning image, tap the blue Camera icon to go back.
A live image of the patient is displayed again.
